sites.home_text:
Aiden Bai 
I’m building Million . We build datasets that teach models to write great frontend code. 
At 16, I created Million.js , a compiler that made React faster. It went viral (Fireship video) and I fell in love with open source. 
Since then I’ve built React Scan , React Grab , and React Doctor ( 45k GitHub stars ) . 
I’m on a mission to fix the web. It’s how great technology reaches everyone, and everything I build (old and new) comes back to that. 
I occasionally write . 
Background lore 
I went to University of Washington in Seattle for 3 months. Then I dropped out to do Y Combinator (W24) 
In high school, I was a part of Hack Club , my home away from home. I also participated in research competitions (ISEF '22 , '21) and won some awards (ACM SAC '23 Best Paper) . 
Along the way, I've worked on (and shut down) on projects like Same and Million Lint . We grew to 400k+ users and millions of $ in revenue. 
Contact 
Hit me up @aidenybai or aiden@million.dev :)

Million Software, Inc. 
Million is a research lab specializing in frontend coding data. 
We build environments and evals for frontier coding agents. Inside them, agents do the work engineers do every day: ship features, deploy applications, and debug issues in codebases they've never seen. 
One of these is React Bench , which scores coding agents on frontend work in real codebases. 
We also open-source developer tools like React Doctor and React Scan . React Doctor has helped developers find issues in their codebases. 
We believe the next generation of software will be built by agents, and we're working to make sure it's actually built well. 
Backed by Scott Wu , Amjad Masad , Evan You , David Cramer , Matt Biilmann , Sam Lambert , Nikita Shamgunov , Sahil Lavingia , Theo Browne , Koen Bok , John Pham , Ben Vinegar , Dane Knecht , Paul Klein IV , and Y Combinator (W24) . 
If this resonates with you, reach out: [email protected] .

#  React Scan
> **You can still use React Scan, but we recommend React Doctor**
>
> React Doctor brings React Scan’s performance focus to coding agents, with static checks for architecture, security, accessibility, and more. [Try React Doctor →](https://react.doctor)
React Scan automatically detects performance issues in your React app.
- Requires no code changes -- just drop it in
- Highlights exactly the components you need to optimize
- Always accessible through a toolbar on page
### Quick Start
```bash
npx -y react-scan@latest init
```
### [**Try out a demo! →**](https://react-scan.million.dev)
## Install
The `init` command will automatically detect your framework, install `react-scan` via npm, and set up your project.
```bash
npx -y react-scan@latest init
```
### Manual Installation
Install the package:
```bash
npm install -D react-scan
```
Then add the script tag to your app. Pick the guide for your framework:
#### Script Tag
Paste this before any scripts in your `index.html`:
```html
<!-- paste this BEFORE any scripts -->
<script
  crossOrigin="anonymous"
  src="//unpkg.com/react-scan/dist/auto.global.js"
></script>
```
#### Next.js (App Router)
Add this inside of your `app/layout.tsx`:
```tsx
import Script from "next/script";
export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
  return (
    <html>
      <head>
        <Script
          src="//unpkg.com/react-scan/dist/auto.global.js"
          crossOrigin="anonymous"
          strategy="beforeInteractive"
        />
      </head>
      <body>{children}</body>
    </html>
  );
}
```
#### Next.js (Pages Router)
Add this into your `pages/_document.tsx`:
```tsx

      </Head>
      <body>
        <Main />
        <NextScript />
      </body>
    </Html>
  );
}
```

React Doctor runs deterministic checks on your code. It reports issues in state and effects, performance, architecture, security, accessibility, and maintainability.
Supports React projects built with Next.js, Vite, Astro, TanStack, React Native, and Expo.
[Documentation →](https://react.doctor/docs)
## Install
### 1. Run a scan
Run this command from your project root:
```bash
npx react-doctor@latest
```
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/07cc88d9-9589-44c3-aa73-5d603cb1c570
### 2. Install for agents
Install the skill to help your coding agent find and fix React issues:
```bash
npx react-doctor@latest install
```
Supports coding agents including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and OpenCode.
### 3. Run in CI
Scan each pull request and report the issues it introduces:
```bash
npx react-doctor@latest ci install
```
[CI docs →](https://react.doctor/ci)
### 4. Configure rules
Choose rules and scan settings in `doctor.config.ts`.
With `customRulesOnly: true`, explicit `rules` settings of `"warn"` or `"error"`
enable selected ported rules. Legacy rule names also work. Other ported rules and
the React Compiler plugin stay off.
[Configuration docs →](https://react.doctor/docs/configuration/config-files)
## Runtime performance traces
Record a Chrome DevTools performance trace while you interact with a running React app:
```bash
npx react-doctor@latest scan http://localhost:3000
```
[Runtime trace docs →](https://react.doctor/docs/reference/cli-reference#runtime-performance-traces)
## Telemetry
The CLI collects crash reports and anonymous usage data. See [Data use](https://react.doctor/docs/legal/data-use) for details.
To opt out, run: `npx react-doctor@latest --no-telemetry`
## Contributing
[Report an issue](https://github.com/millionco/react-doctor/issues)

We don’t recommend depending on them unless you have to.
